content.text:
This is nalidixic acid: 1-ethyl-7-methyl-4-oxo-1,8-naphthyridine-3-carboxylic acid.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- The right ring contains N1 (bearing the ethyl group), C2 (=C3, drawn as a double bond), C3 (bearing COOH), C4 (C=O), C4a and C8a.
- The left ring contains N8, C7 (bearing the methyl), C6, C5, C4a and C8a. The double bonds are N8=C7, C6=C5 and C4a=C8a.

SMILES: CCN1C=C(C(=O)O)C(=O)c2ccc(C)nc21

I wrote the left ring in aromatic notation. In the right ring, C2=C3 is a double bond and C4 is a carbonyl carbon. The ring fusion atoms are c2 (C4a) and c21 (C8a). C8a is bonded to N1 and to N8, which closes the ring.

Atom check: N1 is bonded to the ethyl group, C2 and C8a. C2=C3, and C3 carries the carboxylic acid and bonds to C4. C4 is C(=O) and attaches to c2 (C4a). Then c c are C5 and C6, c(C) is C7 with the methyl, n is N8, and c21 is C8a, which closes both rings. This is consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: CCN1C=C(C(=O)O)C(=O)c2ccc(C)nc21
